claims.text: Adding a controlled amount of carbon to a phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding carbon will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state in a phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 is an example of the relevant phosphorus-containing compositionally complex alloy system.
Rapid-solidification or laser-based processing promotes amorphization in the relevant alloys.
Excessive carbon can cause carbide formation.
Carbon bonds preferentially with particular alloying elements.
Carbon addition modifies short-range atomic ordering.
Carbon-induced changes in short-range ordering inhibit crystalline nucleation.
Carbon doping increases local atomic-network entropy.
Carbon doping disrupts long-range atomic ordering.
Increased local network entropy and disrupted long-range ordering enhance glass formation.
The proposed carbon-induced structural changes retard crystallization during subsequent thermal exposure.
The carbon-doped alloy will have a greater tendency to form an amorphous structure than an undoped baseline.
The carbon-doped alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than the undoped baseline.
The beneficial effect exists only within an optimal carbon-concentration window.
Cooling regimes outside rapid solidification may fail to produce the proposed amorphous enhancement.
A crystallization-onset increase of at least 5% together with greater amorphous character is the proposed criterion for observing the predicted improvement.

contradictions.description: The uncertainty field says the optimal carbon concentration still needs to be determined experimentally, whereas the proposed experiment assumes a predetermined optimal carbon amount without specifying a prior optimization step.
